title: Build real-time multimodal agents with Gemini and Pipecat
transcriptText:
Hey, I'm Chad Bailey.
I'm from the team that builds Pipecat,
the open source framework for
real-time agent orchestration
in multimodal apps.
I've been experimenting with
the new Gemini 3 based
multimodal real-time model,
and I'm excited to show
you what it can do.
Let's go plan a trip to Italy.
- Hello. What kind of
vacation are you dreaming of?
- Well, it's my daughter's
18th birthday coming up
and we told her she could pick
somewhere to go in Europe.
- That's generous. To help narrow it down,
What's she interested in?
Like art, beaches, history or something else?
- Definitely like art and history.
I think we're thinking Italy, possibly.
- Italy's perfect for that. For Art and History,
maybe suggest Rome or Florence?
Rome's got ancient sites. And Florence is packed with Renaissance masterpieces. What do you think?
- Yeah, I was going to say we're
planning on spending about a week.
So I was going to say maybe, like two destinations.
I think Rome and Florence
sounds pretty good.
Great choice. A week gives you roughly
four days in Rome and three in Florence.
To look at flight options, what's your origin city
and what dates are you considering?
We'll be flying from Austin, and we're thinking
probably sometime in July.
- Flying from Austin in July?
There are some flights to
Rome, mostly with one stop.
Prices are roughly between
$580 and $811 per person.
Did you have specific dates in mind,
or would you like to
look for lodging next?
- We're kind of open on dates,
but I'd be curious to know if you could look
at a few days in either direction,
see if there's a difference in airfare.
- Looking around that first week of July,
flights are mostly between $690 and $870.
The cheapest options seem to be around the 1st or 3rd of July.
Would you like to explore lodging now,
or should we look at more flight options?
- Yeah. Let's plan on starting the trip on the third for now.
Let's talk about lodging.
- Great. Starting July 3rd.
- Are you looking for
hotels, Airbnb, or VRBO?
And for how many guests?
Do you want to stay in Rome first or Florence?
- I’m not sure which one we want to do first.
There's going to  be five of us,
so I don't know if there's hotel rooms that are big enough for us,
so maybe let's look for hotels,
but also we can check Airbnb.
For a group of five,
checking both hotels and Airbnbs is a good idea.
- Since you were looking
at flights to Rome,
how about we search there first
for say, July 3rd to 7th?
Then we can compare. Sound good?
- Okay. Yeah.
- In Rome from July 3rd to 7th
for hotels, you can find
some places like
the Hyatt Grand Rome
for around $138 per night,
though its rating is a bit lower.
The Four Seasons has a better
rating at roughly $191.
For Airbnbs, there's a
penthouse for $114 per night
with good reviews or larger
places like a cottage for around $166.
Should we look at specific areas
or maybe search lodging in Florence?
- I mean, let's--I probably want something
like centrally located in Rome.
Is that penthouse, like is the--
which of those Airbnb listings is
closer to like center of town?
- I've just searched again for Airbnbs,
specifically in the central Rome area.
You can find a modern loft
for about $227 a night
or a stylish flat with good
reviews for around $247.
Does that sound closer
to what you had in mind?
- Yeah. Let's do a loft. That sounds good.
There's a lot of new functionality
sprinkled throughout there.
So let me show you how I built this bot
and we'll look at some of
the new things that Gemini 3
adds in along the way.
Now, the easiest way to
scaffold the new voice agent is
with the Pipecat CLI.
You can install that by running
uv tool install pipecat-ai-cli
Of course, I've already
got it installed.
Now I'll run Pipecat
init to create a new bot.
I’ll call it Gemini demo.
And you have a lot of flexibility here.
With Pipecat you can pick your transport.
I'm using the web because
it's an easier demo,
but you can hook this up directly
to your telephony provider.
You can even create a
WhatsApp voice business agent,
all that kind of stuff.
You can deploy to
Pipecat Cloud if you want,
but Pipecat is totally open
source and vendor neutral.
You can run your bot on your
own infrastructure
on Google Cloud platform
or really whatever you want
with no external dependencies.
Once that's done, I'll go off screen
to set up environment variables.
Just for a second,
I'm starting from a very
standard Pipecat bot file here.
If you're not familiar with Pipecat,
you can visit pipecat.ai to
learn all about the framework.
For now, I'm going to
get right into building
what we just saw.
First things first, we need
to configure this bot
to use the new model.
Now I'm making one other
important change here.
I'm setting the thinking level to minimal.
I know it sounds kind of funny
to ask the model to think
as little as possible when it talks to us,
but this has a really big impact on
how quickly the bot will answer us,
and it turns out that
Gemini 3 is more than smart enough
to do all of this without having
to think too hard about it.
Now we get to the first big
improvement with Gemini 3.
It's way better at instruction following.
That means I can drop
in a gigantic system prompt
and Gemini 3 will do a
much better job at staying on
task even in very long conversations.
Pipecat has a module called
Pipecat Flows that you can use
to guide models through
complex multi-step workflows,
but as the models get
better, you can get away
with just telling it everything you need
to do upfront in the system prompt.
In fact, all the snippets
you're seeing are
from me having 15 minute
conversations with this bot
and it stays on topic the entire time.
Next, another important
improvement in Gemini 3,
greatly improved tool
calling capabilities.
This is important for any
voice agent that needs
to do anything other than talking,
which is pretty much any voice agent
that's actually worth using.
There are a few tools
we'll need for this bot.
First, searching for flights.
For now, I'm going to
just return hard coded
data for some of this stuff.
Here's how you define
function call handlers in Pipecat.
Now to start, I've got this
generate mock flights function
to make some fake data.
This search flights function is
what actually does the flight
lookup when the LLM uses the
search flights tool.
This search flight schema
object is how we tell the LLM.
It has a tool called search
flights and how to use it.
Then we put that in a tool schema
and we register it with the LLM down here.
Now you can read a lot
more about this at pipecat.ai.
I'm going to go ahead and add
a lodging tool as well.
Same idea: mock data,
because I can't be bothered
with a real API in a live demo.
Tell Pipecat how to do it.
Describe the tool for the LLM.
Then tell the LLM it can
use it when it wants to.
Then finally connect
the LLM's idea of the tool
to Pipecat's handler function.
Now, in my opinion, one
of the marquee features
of the Gemini models is their
Google Search grounding.
I can add that to the bot just like this.
This one is easy. Gemini
already knows how to use Google.
This is basically just turning it on.
Now, I'd hate to spend all
this time talking to this bot
to plan this trip and have
nothing to show for it.
Fortunately, Gemini 3 is multimodal.
I'm going to  add a tool call
to save a trip report.
- Welcome back. We were looking at flights
from Austin to Rome in July of 2026.
Should we finalize those dates or
look for lodging in Rome or Florence?
- Yeah. I think based on the festival and stuff,
it sounds like we're sort of orbiting around
some dates we might be able to use.
- Got it. Around July 21st to 28th, roughly a week?
Want to solidify those dates for flight searching?
Or maybe look at that downtown
townhouse in Rome for lodging?
- Yeah, let’s--actually, now that we know dates,
let’s look at Rome lodging options.
- I found some great options for your family
in Rome from July 21st to 24th.
For Airbnbs, there's a modern loft with
a rooftop terrace for about $181 a night,
and a treehouse retreat further out for $294.
If you prefer a hotel, the Hyatt Harbor
is around $207 a night with great reviews,
or the Four Seasons offers more luxury and a pool at $380.
Any of those sound interesting,
or would you like me to filter by something else?
- Definitely want a pool.
That sounds good. It's going to be hot.
- A pool is a great call for July.
The Four Seasons Park Rome Hotel
has one for about $136 a night.
On Airbnb, there's a charming cottage
with a pool for $268, though it's a bit more.
Do either of those work or would you
like to look more at a specific price range?
- Let's do the cottage.
That sounds good.
And go ahead and--let's go ahead and save this out.
I think, I need to go do some other stuff,
so let's save what we got.
- Saved.
The current plan with the charming
cottage in Rome is all set.
Safe travels and let me
know when you're ready
to start planning activities or flights.
- Cool, thanks.
For that, I'll have the
model return markdown text
describing everything we've
planned for the trip so far.
Then when I see that text response,
I'll just save it to disc.
It looks like this.
This is from my earlier conversation.
I can even read this back into the context
when I start another session.
To pick up where we left off.
Since I'm planning a trip to Italy,
I want to practice my
non-existent Italian skills
Before I go.
I'm going to  add
another agent into this bot file
using a new Pipecat
module called Pipecat Agents.
This module lets me run multiple agents
inside a single bot file
and it handles things
like a shared message bus
between the agents for me.
Let's go ahead and add
that to the code now.
There's kind of a lot here,
but at a high level, we define
a Gemini Live agent class.
Each instance of this
will contain its own pipeline
with its own LLM service and
registered tool calls and such.
There's this handle transfer function
that Pipecat agents will wire up for us.
And then we have two
subclasses: concierge agent
and language tutor agent with
different system prompts.
And then the run bot function
actually uses this agent runner
to run both of those agents
and connect them together
with a messaging bus.
This bot can do so much
and we've only just scratched the surface
of what's possible with Gemini 3.
Head over to this Google link
to learn more about
what the model can do
then head to pipecat.ai
to start building your bot.
